summary: Partial expression indexes on the email correlation keys in the objects.data JSONB column (cinatra#1456): objects_data_thread_idx ON objects(org_id,(data->>'threadId')) WHERE data->>'threadId' IS NOT NULL; objects_data_campaign_idx ON objects(org_id,(data->>'campaignId')) WHERE data->>'campaignId' IS NOT NULL; objects_data_contact_idx ON objects(org_id,(data->>'connectorId'),(data->>'contactId')) WHERE data->>'contactId' IS NOT NULL. WHY: the #1456 indexed thread/campaign/contact query seam (src/lib/email-correlation-queries.ts) filters the email transport records (email:sent-email/received-reply/recipient) by the correlation ids that live in the JSONB data column, via listObjectsByFilter's allow-listed dataEquals filter (compiles to data->>'<key>' = $n); those columns had no index, so the views would sequential-scan without these. Partial (WHERE key IS NOT NULL) so only correlation-carrying rows enter each index (tiny+selective); jsonb ->> text is IMMUTABLE so it is index-expression-eligible; the contact index leads with (org_id,connectorId,contactId) because a provider-native contactId is only meaningful within its connector so the view filters the pair. Additive: the bootstrap DDL (buildEmailCorrelationIndexQueries spliced into buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries in src/lib/drizzle-store.ts, same PR) creates them via CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS so a fresh install is born at the target shape and ledger-fakes this chain; this module carries the same creates onto the operator upgrade path (core__0050 convention). BACKFILL: also runs an idempotent forward-only UPDATE that derives data.threadId = connectorId||':'||providerThreadId on historical @cinatra-ai/email:sent-email rows that carry a providerThreadId but no threadId yet (the writer only began emitting the derived key in this PR; received-reply already carried it), so the thread query seam sees historical sends. jsonb_set is additive (sets a previously-null key, no data loss); the WHERE makes it a no-op on re-run and on a fresh install with no such rows. Idempotent both ways; unqualified names resolve to the runner's search_path schema. down() drops the three indexes IF EXISTS (a pure performance revert, no data loss). SEQ PROVISIONAL: assigned at MERGE (the gate requires new seq > max SHIPPED, currently 0060); this fragment takes 0061 — the next free sequence past max shipped; a concurrent lane may claim 0061 first, in which case renumber-at-merge is normal (rename-only, zero SQL change; the runner tolerates gaps). migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges.
